title: Quotient-tower inflation and identity coherence on resolutions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$, write $\mathcal A_P(A)$ for internal $A$-modules with condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and $\Gamma_P$ for sections fixed after every profinite base change. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $P_0\xrightarrow{p_1}P_1\xrightarrow{p_2}P_2$ be quotient projections of profinite groups with open normal kernels; a further profinite factor $L$ is allowed and each projection then acts as the identity on $L$. Put $T_1(M)=M^{\ker p_1}$, $T_2(M)=M^{\ker p_2}$ and $T_{02}(M)=M^{\ker(p_2p_1)}$, retaining the respective residual actions. Use normalized invariant inclusions, inflation adjunctions, derived comparison $c$ and derived inflation with the resolution formulas of [def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data, lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality]. On objects and maps, $T_{02}=T_2T_1$ and the inclusion $\operatorname{Inf}_{02}T_{02}M\to M$ is the composite of the two invariant inclusions. For a K-injective $I$ in $\mathcal A_{P_0\times L}(A)$, $T_1I$ and $T_2T_1I$ are K-injective, and the derived composition comparisons in either parenthesization are the identity on
$$I^{P_0\times L}=(T_1I)^{P_1\times L}=(T_2T_1I)^{P_2\times L}.$$
These equalities of canonical comparisons hold naturally for all unbounded derived objects.

For every module $N$ in $\mathcal A_{P_0\times L}(A)$, the actual derived inflation arrows satisfy
$$\operatorname{inf}_{02,N}=\operatorname{inf}_{1,N}\circ\operatorname{inf}_{2,T_1N},$$
where $T_{02}N$ is identified with $T_2T_1N$. Its resolution normalization is the following precise assertion. Given K-injective resolutions $i:N[0]\to I$, $a:T_1N[0]\to J$, $z:T_2T_1N[0]\to Z$, choose homotopy classes $b:J\to T_1I$, $d:Z\to T_2J$ with $ba\simeq T_1(i)$ and $dz\simeq T_2(a)$. Then $T_2(b)d:Z\to T_2T_1I$ is the unique homotopy class extending $T_2T_1(i)$ along $z$, and its full $P_2\times L$-invariants represent both the direct inflation and the composite inflation.

For a quotient with trivial kernel, the functor $T$ is the identity and the unit $\eta_N$, the kernel comparison $\beta$ and the composition comparison $c$ are identities under the canonical exact-functor identifications. All assertions include the zero ring, zero module, a quotient to the trivial group and trivial $L$, with no division by group orders.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker p_1$ and $H=\ker(p_2p_1)$. These are open normal subgroups of $P_0$, and $p_1(H)=\ker p_2$. Use the continuous set section of $p_1$ supplied by [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models]. For a section $m$ of $M$ fixed by $H$ after every profinite base change, it is fixed by $K$. Every generalized element $v$ of $\ker p_2$ lifts through that section to an $H$-valued generalized element, so the residual action fixes $m$. Conversely, if $m$ is $K$-fixed and its residual action is fixed by $\ker p_2$, an $H$-valued generalized element acts as its image under $p_1$, hence fixes $m$. This proves $T_{02}M=T_2T_1M$ as submodules of $M$ with their normalized inclusions. The residual $P_2\times L$-actions agree because both are induced by lifts in $P_0\times L$. An equivariant map restricts to the same map of these submodules in either construction, so the equality is functorial. Both inflated inclusions send a fixed section to that very section of $M$; their composite is the direct inclusion. The same argument, with all elements instead of kernel elements, gives $\Gamma_{P_0\times L}=\Gamma_{P_1\times L}T_1=\Gamma_{P_2\times L}T_2T_1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models] to $p_1$, $p_2$ and $p_2p_1$, using their specified quotient identifications. The first two kernels are open normal by hypothesis; the third is $H=p_1^{-1}(\ker p_2)$, hence open normal as well. The lemma permits the unchanged factor $L$ and supplies K-injective resolutions in each action category. It says that $T_1$, $T_2$ and $T_{02}$ preserve K-injectives. In particular $T_1I$ and then $T_2T_1I$ are K-injective, and $T_2J$ is K-injective whenever $J$ is. Thus every target of a resolution lift used below has the required K-injectivity.

proof.text: Use the composition comparison of [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality] for each projection and for the composite. On the common K-injective representative $I$, its normalization is the identity on the full-invariant complex. In computing the iterated comparison no new resolution is needed, by step 2. By step 1 all complexes in the two paths are the same subcomplex $I^{P_0\times L}$. Each path is therefore a composite of identity chain maps on this subcomplex, so the paths agree with the direct comparison, including either parenthesization.

proof.text: For the specified resolutions $i,a,z$, apply [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality] first to $p_1$ with resolutions $i,a$, and then to $p_2$ with resolutions $a,z$. This supplies $b:J\to T_1I$ and $d:Z\to T_2J$ with $ba\simeq T_1(i)$ and $dz\simeq T_2(a)$. Their targets $T_1I$ and $T_2J$ are K-injective by step 2. Additive functors act termwise on homotopies, so $T_2(b)d\,z\simeq T_2(b)T_2(a)=T_2(ba)\simeq T_2T_1(i)$. Put $B=T_2T_1I$, also K-injective by step 2. For both sources $Z$ and $T_2T_1N[0]$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies homotopy Hom into $B$ with derived Hom. Precomposition by $Qz$ is bijective since $z$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the localization map therefore makes precomposition by $z$ bijective on these homotopy Hom sets. Hence $T_2(b)d$ is the unique homotopy class extending $T_2T_1(i)$. Neither $T_2(a)$ nor $T_1(i)$ is assumed to be a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality], $\operatorname{inf}_{2,T_1N}$ is represented by $\Gamma_{P_2\times L}(d):\Gamma_{P_2\times L}Z\to\Gamma_{P_1\times L}J$, and $\operatorname{inf}_{1,N}$ by $\Gamma_{P_1\times L}(b):\Gamma_{P_1\times L}J\to\Gamma_{P_0\times L}I$. The identifications of step 1 hold on maps, so the second chain map is also $\Gamma_{P_2\times L}(T_2b)$. Their composite is therefore $\Gamma_{P_2\times L}(T_2(b)d)$. The direct inflation, by the same single-projection formula for $p_2p_1$ and the uniqueness in step 4, is represented by exactly this map. Homotopic lifts remain homotopic after the additive full-invariant functor. Hence the two actual derived arrows agree, as required.

proof.text: The single-projection formula [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality] is independent of resolutions and natural in module maps; thus the equality in step 5 has these same properties. For the comparison identities on all unbounded derived objects, choose K-injective representatives using step 2. Every derived morphism between these representatives is represented by a chain map unique up to homotopy, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Full invariants and iterated kernel invariants restrict that chain map to the identical fixed subcomplexes of step 1; identity chain maps commute with those restrictions. Changing K-injective representatives gives an isomorphism represented by mutually inverse homotopy classes, again by the cited Hom bijection. The additive invariant functors preserve their homotopies and hence these inverses. The same restriction calculation therefore proves independence of representatives as well as naturality of step 3 for every unbounded derived morphism.

proof.text: If the kernel is trivial, every section is kernel-fixed, so its normalized invariant inclusion identifies $T$ with the identity, after transport along the quotient group isomorphism. For any resolution $i:X\to I$, the unit defined in [def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data] is represented by $i$; under the canonical exact-identity-functor identification this is the identity of $QX$. The formulas of [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models] and [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality] represent $\beta$ and $c$ by identities on the same complexes, so they too are identities. The argument used only invariant inclusions, functoriality and K-injective comparison. It therefore also applies to the zero ring and zero module, to a quotient onto the trivial group, and to trivial $L$; no averaging or group-order inversion occurs.
